e.etymology: A respelling of Isabella, the Spanish and Italian form of Isabel, which grew out of the medieval form of Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath.
The Polish form of Luke and Lucas, from Greek Loukas, a man from Lucania in southern Italy. In Polish it is written with a barred L, which sounds like English w.
In South Asia from hira, diamond, a word that goes back to Sanskrit. Muslim families also choose it for the Cave of Hira near Mecca, where Muhammad is said to have received his first revelation.
A name with several unrelated sources: Hebrew chai, alive or living; Thai chai, victory; and Chinese and Hmong names written Chai in English. Chai is also the Hindi word for tea.
Modern Hebrew ma'ayan, a spring or fountain. It is used in Israel for both girls and boys.
From Arabic salih, righteous or pious. In the Quran Salih is the prophet sent to the people of Thamud.
Used mainly in Spanish-speaking and Filipino families. Its source is not established; reference works group it with Saira and Shara.
The English word, from Old English thunor, which is related to the name of the Norse god Thor. Its use as a given name is recent.
A modern American name built from Ry-, as in Riley and Ryan, and the ending -lynn. It is also used as a feminine spelling of Rylan.
The South Asian form of Arabic Ridwan, good pleasure or acceptance, especially God's. In Islamic tradition Ridwan is also the angel who keeps the gates of Paradise.
namesakes: Riz Ahmed (Oscar-nominated actor, born Rizwan Ahmed)

e.etymology: A modern spelling in the family of Leia, Laya and Laia; how it is said varies from family to family.

A Chinese given name whose meaning depends on the character chosen; common ones mean joyful, resolute, art and righteousness. Yi is also a Chinese surname and one English spelling of the Korean surname Lee.
A modern American coinage joining Drey, a spelling of Dre or Trey, to the -son ending of Greyson and Bryson.
Used mainly in South Asian families, alongside similar names such as Eshan, Ehsan and Ayaan. Its derivation is not well documented.
The Finnish form of Elsie and a pet form of Elsa, both short forms of Elizabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. In the United States it is mostly a spelling of Elsie or Elsy.
Hebrew elah, the terebinth or oak tree. In the Bible Elah is a king of Israel and the valley where David fought Goliath; in modern Hebrew, written Ela, it is a girl's name.
A modern American coinage joining Kash, a spelling of Cash, to the ending -lyn, in the pattern of Ashlyn and Kaitlyn.
A modern American spelling in the style of Zyra, Zara and Kyra, with no older source of its own.
Hebrew adir, mighty or majestic, a word the Bible uses of God and of great waters. Adir Hu, Mighty is He, is a hymn sung at the Passover seder.
A short form of longer names, among them Romanian Octavian and Scottish Tavish, also used on its own. Kipling's mongoose Rikki-Tikki-Tavi carries it too.
A surname and a pet form of Dallas. In rodeo, to dally is to wrap the rope around the saddle horn after roping a steer, which gives the name a western flavor.
namesakes: Dally Winston (Dallas Winston, the tough greaser in The Outsiders)
e.note: As an ordinary English verb, dally means to dawdle or to flirt.

e.etymology: The English word, from Greek prophetes, one who speaks on behalf of a god. It joined Messiah, Saint and Legend as a given name in the 2010s; Prophet is also an English surname.

e.meaning: son of Wilk, a pet form of William
e.etymology: An English surname meaning son of Wilk, a short form of Wilkin, itself a medieval pet form of William. William is Germanic, from will, desire, and helm, helmet.

assoc.t: John Wilkes Booth, assassin of Abraham Lincoln

e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Nyla and Nylah, written with the ending of Leah.
A recent American coinage that extends the Azar- of Azariah with the ending of Orion and Darion.
A feminine form of Azriel, a Hebrew name made of azar, help, and El, God, with the ending of Ariella and Gabriella.
A modern American coinage of the 2010s in the family of Brexley, Braxley and Brinley, with the -lee ending.
A spelling of Hebrew Ilai, from an Aramaic word for upper or exalted. Ilai is one of King David's warriors in the Bible. A separate Turkish girl's name is spelled the same way.
Arabic ilaf, familiarity or accord, a word from the opening of Surah Quraysh in the Quran, where it refers to the safe arrangements that protected the tribe's trading caravans.
A respelling of Ariella, the feminine form of Ariel, from Hebrew ari, lion, and El, God. In the Bible Ariel is a poetic name for Jerusalem.
A modern coinage in the style of Dylan, Rylan and Zylan with the fashionable initial X. Xylan is also the name of a compound found in plant fiber.
